elements.label: Figure 7.10

Two vertical bar charts (point change) showing the impact of fiscal policy on inequality by country income level. Bars are teal, with Vietnam highlighted in orange. Countries are grouped by income level: High income, Upper middle income, Lower middle income, and Lower income. Y-axis title: 'Point change'.

Panel A: Excluding in-kind spending on health and education. Y-axis from -8 to 2. Approximate readings (~) by country, in order:
- High income: Poland ~-5.7, Romania ~-4.2, Croatia ~-3.7, Uruguay ~-3.7, Chile ~-3.0, Panama ~-2.8
- Upper middle income: South Africa ~-7.7, Argentina ~-6.4, Iran ~-5.7, Namibia ~-4.5, Mexico ~-3.8, Mexico ~-3.8, Ecuador ~-3.3, Brazil ~-3.1, Mexico ~-3.0, Russia ~-2.8, Armenia ~-2.8, Albania ~-2.4, Belarus ~-2.2, Costa Rica ~-2.2, Dominican Republic ~-2.2, Venezuela ~-2.1, Colombia ~-1.9, Jordan ~-1.6, Colombia ~-1.6, Peru ~-1.3, Peru ~-1.2, Paraguay ~-1.2, Indonesia ~-0.8, Guatemala ~-0.7
- Lower middle income: Ukraine ~-6.4, Tunisia ~-5.0, Tanzania ~-4.0, Kenya ~-3.4, El Salvador ~-3.1, Vietnam ~-2.9, Egypt ~-2.6, Nicaragua ~-1.7, Ghana ~-1.4, Honduras ~-1.2, Sri Lanka ~-0.6, Bolivia ~0 (bar not clearly visible), Comoros ~+1.3
- Lower income: Ethiopia ~-2.0, Uganda ~-1.6, Burkina Faso ~-1.0
Most countries show negative (equalizing) impacts; Comoros is the only clear positive bar, and South Africa and Ukraine show the largest reductions in the panel.

Panel B: Including in-kind spending on health and education. Y-axis from -25 to 0. Approximate readings (~) by country, in order:
- High income: Poland ~-12.0, Croatia ~-10.0, Panama ~-8.8, Uruguay ~-8.6, Chile ~-7.3, Romania ~-7.0
- Upper middle income: Namibia ~-20.5, Argentina ~-17.5, South Africa ~-17.5, Costa Rica ~-10.5, Brazil ~-9.3, Mexico ~-8.6, Iran ~-8.5, Mexico ~-8.3, Mexico ~-8.0, Ecuador ~-7.3, Belarus ~-6.5, Colombia ~-6.3, Colombia ~-6.0, Venezuela ~-5.8, Russia ~-5.5, Albania ~-5.1, Dominican Republic ~-5.2, Paraguay ~-4.8, Armenia ~-4.6, Peru ~-4.2, Peru ~-3.7, Indonesia ~-2.6, Guatemala ~-2.3, Jordan ~-2.1

Note: Pensions treated as deferred income. Source: CEQ and World Bank databases and World Bank calculations (see Rodriguez and Wai-Poi, 2020).
